sentences.text: Australovenator was a dinosaur approximately 6 meters long that stood about 2 meters high at the hip.
Its body mass is estimated to have ranged between 310 and 500 kilograms, with Gregory S. Paul specifically estimating 500 kilograms in 2016.
The name Australovenator combines the Latin words for 'southern' and 'hunter', referencing its location and diet.
Although no skull is known, Australovenator likely had an elongated, slender head similar to other megaraptorans.
The dentary bone of Australovenator is long and measures 342.6 mm in length as preserved.
The humerus of Australovenator is S-shaped and bears a prominent deltopectoral crest.
Australovenator possessed a giant, recurved hand claw, a trait characteristic of the megaraptoran clade.
It was a relatively lightweight predator, earning it the nickname 'cheetah of its time'.
Australovenator's phalanx II-3 was splayed, possibly due to impacts from kicking motions.
The holotype specimen of Australovenator was discovered near Elderslie Station in 2006.
Scott Hocknull and colleagues published a description of Australovenator in the journal PLOS One in 2009.
The holotype specimen includes elements such as both lower jaws, many teeth, ribs, arm and leg bones, and foot bones.
Researchers suggest Australovenator used its flexible arms to grasp prey for its weak jaws to disembowel.
A 2013 review re-identified several incorrectly positioned phalanges in Australovenator.
The environment where Australovenator lived was humid with about 74% relative humidity and significant seasonal rainfall.
Summers in Australovenator's habitat were hot at about 21°C, while moderate seasons ranged from approximately 9°C to -2°C.
Australovenator belongs to the clade Megaraptora, which existed during the Cretaceous in Asia, South America, and Oceania.
Australovenator is classified within the family Megaraptoridae.
Australovenator was initially classified within the superfamily Allosauroidea due to sharing many characteristics with primitive allosauroids.
Some researchers have suggested that Rapator might be the closest relative (sister taxon) of Australovenator.
Australovenator lived during the early Late Cretaceous, approximately 95 million years ago in the Cenomanian stage, in what is now Australia.
The Winton Formation's sandstone suggests an environment dominated by oxbow lakes or similar lacustrine settings.
The holotype was recovered from the lower part of the Winton Formation, dated to the late Albian.
Australovenator lived between 125.77 and 89.8 million years ago, during the Barremian to Turonian stages.
The higher-level classification relationships of the group Megaraptora remain uncertain.
It is debated whether Megaraptora, including Australovenator, are carcharodontosaurs, basal coelurosaurs, or tyrannosauroids.
A 2016 study suggested Australovenator could be an allosauroid or a basal coelurosaur.
A recent phylogenetic analysis suggests Australovenator is a tyrannosauroid, similar to all other megaraptorids.
It is debated whether Rapator and Australovenator are the same species, with some researchers arguing they are distinct due to age and morphological differences.
A specimen from the Winton Formation shows differences from Australovenator, leading to debates about whether it represents a different species, age-related changes, or individual variation.
